facts.statement: Rhabdognathus possessed an extremely elongated snout comprising approximately 75% of the total skull length.
facts.quote: Rhabdognathus has an extremely elongated snout that makes up around 75% of the length of the entire skull.

facts.statement: The total skull length of the species Rhabdognathus keiniensis was 73.1 centimeters.
facts.quote: The total skull length of R. keiniensis is 73.1 cm

facts.statement: The mandible of Rhabdognathus was as high as it was wide or even higher, a feature distinguishing it from Hyposaurus.
facts.quote: The mandible of Rhabdognathus is as high as it is wide or higher, which distinguishes it from Hyposaurus.

facts.statement: A distinguishing feature of Rhabdognathus was an extremely long mandibular symphysis extending past the nineteenth tooth socket.
facts.quote: Another distinguishing feature is the extreme length of the mandibular symphysis, which extends past the nineteenth mandibular alveolus.

facts.statement: Rhabdognathus was named by Swinton in 1930 based on a lower jaw fragment found in Nigeria.
facts.quote: It was named by Swinton in 1930 for a lower jaw fragment from Nigeria.

facts.statement: Specimens of Rhabdognathus dating back to the Maastrichtian era were identified in 2008.
facts.quote: specimens dating back to the Maastrichtian era were identified in 2008

facts.statement: Two skulls originally assigned to Rhabdognathus were reclassified as new species, R. aslerensis and R. keiniensis, both found in Mali.
facts.quote: Two skulls which were assigned to the genus Rhabdognathus but which could not be shown to be identical to R. rarus were given new species: R. aslerensis and R. keiniensis, both from Mali.

facts.statement: The species Rhabdognathus compressus was reassigned to the genus Congosaurus after analysis showed its lower jaw was more similar to Congosaurus bequaerti.
facts.quote: The genus formerly contained the species Rhabdognathus compressus, which was reassigned to Congosaurus compressus after analysis of the lower jaw of a specimen found that it was more similar to that of the species Congosaurus bequaerti.

facts.statement: Rhabdognathus is believed to be the closest relative to the extinct genus Atlantosuchus.
facts.quote: Rhabdognathus is believed to be the closest relative to the extinct Atlantosuchus.

facts.statement: Rhabdognathus fossils are known from rocks of the Paleocene epoch in western Africa.
facts.quote: It is known from rocks dating to the Paleocene epoch from western Africa

facts.statement: Rhabdognathus lived from the Maastrichtian to the Thanetian, between 72.2 and 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Thanetian (72.2 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: Stéphane Jouve assessed the type species R. rarus as dubious because it was indeterminate at the species level.
facts.quote: Stéphane Jouve subsequently assessed R. rarus as indeterminate at the species level, but not at the genus level, and thus dubious.

rejected.statement: The tooth sockets of Rhabdognathus were rounded and angled slightly outward, causing the teeth to project at an angle.
rejected.quote: The alveoli of Rhabdognathus are rounded and directed slightly laterally, causing the teeth to project at an angle.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'causing the teeth to project at an angle'

rejected.statement: Rhabdognathus is an extinct genus of dyrosaurid crocodylomorph.
rejected.quote: Rhabdognathus is an extinct genus of dyrosaurid crocodylomorph.
